## FilterDSL

<span class="api-kind">namespace</span>

Imported as a namespace, and re-exported member by member from a second entry point.

### FilterDSL.CNode

```ts
type CNode = FieldNode | ConditionNode | ValueNode | ValuesNode | OperationNode | ComponentNode;
```

### FilterDSL.ComponentNode

```ts
interface ComponentNode
```

Component node. Wraps another condition. Think of it like a named term.

`type: "Component"`

`id: string | null` -- Id of the component

`condition: CNode` -- Actual condition

### FilterDSL.ComputedValue

```ts
type ComputedValue = {
  name: string;
  args: RawValue[];
};
```

### FilterDSL.Condition

```ts
type Condition = ConditionNode & { [K in keyof typeof CONDITION_METHODS]: CondFn<(typeof CONDITION_METHODS)[K]>; };
```

### FilterDSL.ConditionNode

```ts
interface ConditionNode
```

Named condition Node.

`type: "Condition"`

`name: string` -- Name of the condition (e.g. "greater")

`operands: CNode[]` -- Operands of the condition

### FilterDSL.Field

```ts
type Field = FieldNode & FieldConditions & FieldOperations;
```

### FilterDSL.FieldExpression

```ts
type FieldExpression = string | CNode;
```

### FilterDSL.FieldNode

```ts
interface FieldNode
```

Field reference.

`type: "Field"`

`name: string` -- Name of the field

### FilterDSL.FilterExpression

```ts
type FilterExpression = ConditionNode | ComponentNode;
```

A composed filter: a condition, or a component marker wrapping one. This is
what a filter *is* - it never includes falsy members.

### FilterDSL.LogicalOperand

```ts
type LogicalOperand = FilterExpression | null | undefined | false;
```

What or() / and() *accept*. Falsy operands are dropped, which is the point of
the logical composers: callers compose from helpers that may contribute
nothing and let the final logical shape fall out of whatever survived.

Note that `flag && cond` only lands in this type when `flag` is a boolean.
For a truthy-narrowable value use `!!flag && cond`, or the equivalent
`flag ? cond : null` - `"" | undefined | Condition` is not an operand.

### FilterDSL.OperationNode

```ts
interface OperationNode
```

Operation node. Addition, subtraction etc.

`type: "Operation"`

`name: string` -- Name of the operation

`operands: CNode[]` -- Operands of the operation

### FilterDSL.RawValue

```ts
type RawValue = null | string | number | boolean | RawValue[] | {

};
```

JSON value equivalent

### FilterDSL.Value


### FilterDSL.ValueNode

```ts
interface ValueNode
```

Value node. Represents a single runtime-typed value.

`type: "Value"`

`scalarType: string` -- Scalar type of the value

`value: RawValue` -- Raw/json value

### FilterDSL.ValuesNode

```ts
interface ValuesNode
```

Values node. Represents an array of values.

`type: "Values"`

`scalarType: string` -- Scalar type of the elements in the value array

`values: RawValue[]` -- Array of raw values.

### FilterDSL.and

```ts
declare const and: (...args: LogicalOperand[]) => (FilterExpression | null);
```

Logical and condition. Will ignore falsy operands. An empty and collapses to null.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `{...` | CNode} operands |

**Returns** {CNode} ANDed condition

### FilterDSL.component()

```ts
declare function component(id: string | null, condition: CNode): ComponentNode;
```

Component condition node. These nodes are just marker for which part of the condition originated from which component
Logically they are evaluated as the condition they wrap.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `{String}` | id                   component id |
| `{CNode}` | condition     actual condition for the component  |

**Returns** {CNode}

### FilterDSL.toJSON()

```ts
declare function toJSON(condition: CNode): RawValue;
```

Converts the given condition graph into simple js objects.

The Filter DSL produces Filter nodes that are in fact instances of the Filter DSL types used to implement to
conditions/operations. This works fine in many cases, but sometimes it doesn't.

One example is that mobx will ignore the instances and not create observables for them. Making the FilterDSL in general
observable would be possible, but would mean a huge overhead for a very exotic use-case.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `condition` | Input condition, potentially consisting of DSL instances |

**Returns** condition as graph of objects / arrays

## decompileFilter()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function decompileFilter(condition: CNode | null, level?: number, match?: CNode | null, invert?: boolean): string;
```

Converts the given FilterDSL condition graph into a pretty-formatted source
form using the FilterDSL API (and DateTime.fromIso() expressions)

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `{Object}` | condition        condition graph |
| `{Number}` | level            starting indentation level |
| `{Object}` | match            Optional object to mark. The given node is assumed to an instance in the graph and the source output of that object is marked is enclosed in \/*>>*\/ \/*<<*\/ to mark the object |
| `{boolean}` | invert          inverts condition output (mostly internal usage)  |

**Returns** {string} pretty-printed source string. If match was used, the >> << might prevent it from being valid JavaScript
